# Test fixtures

## `synthetic-raw-capture.jsonl`

**Synthetic. Not captured from any real device.** Every value in it is invented.

It is a stand-in for what a Solar Assistant unit might publish over thirty minutes, written by hand from the documented topic layout and from topic names other users have posted publicly (see [`docs/research/solar-assistant-mqtt.md`](../../../../docs/research/solar-assistant-mqtt.md)). The noise on the values came from a seeded random generator, run once; the file is the fixture, and is not regenerated by the build.

The format is the one `sa-tap record --raw-log` writes: one received MQTT message per line, with its receive time, topic, payload and retained flag. Lines starting with `#` are comments. A capture from a real unit can sit beside this file and be run through the same tests.

What it holds:

| Part | Why it is there |
| --- | --- |
| Six retained discovery configs, one using Home Assistant's short field names and `~` shorthand | Units declared by the source |
| A discovery config for an unrelated device, and a damaged one | Must be ignored, not stored |
| `pv_power` for `inverter_1` and `inverter_2` every 10 s | The two inputs for the ratio monitor |
| A ramp from 60 W over the first five minutes | Pairs below the minimum power |
| A brief dip on both inputs at minute 12 | A passing cloud: the median should not react |
| A ratio near 1.25 for twenty minutes, then near 1.39 | A shift for the monitor to report as drift |
| 150 s with no messages at all | A gap for `replay` to find |
| Voltages, load, frequency, temperature, battery values every 30 s | Units guessed from names; one temperature with no declared unit |
| Text values (`Solar/Battery`, `Load first`) | Non-numeric payloads are ignored and counted |
| A `/set` and a `/set_verified` message from "another client", and a set response | Command topics never become readings |
| One retained state message | Marked as being of unknown age |
| An empty payload, `53.2.1`, `NaN`, `1.2e3 W` | Damaged values |
| Topics of the wrong shape, a name with a space, a topic from another device | Unknown topics |
| A text payload shaped like an instruction | Outside text stays data |

Parts of the layout used here are assumptions, not documented facts: the `inverter_2` and `battery_1` device segments, the payload of the status topic, the exact discovery topic paths, and whether state messages are ever retained.
